top_story: Disruption in the Strait of Hormuz is choking one of the world’s most critical energy corridors, putting roughly a fifth of global crude and LNG flows at risk and quickly translating military escalation into economic shock far beyond the Gulf. U.S. strikes on military targets on Iran’s Kharg Island push that escalation closer to the infrastructure that anchors Iran’s oil exports, increasing the danger of retaliatory action that could further imperil shipping and regional livelihoods tied to energy trade. Trump’s threat to bomb Iranian civilian infrastructure introduces a sharper legal and moral fault line, raising the prospect of unlawful targeting and placing U.S. officers under pressure to weigh obedience against the laws of war. The emerging picture is of a conflict widening from deterrence into coercive economic warfare, with civilians, energy-dependent societies, and already fragile regional stability likely to absorb the heaviest costs.
